analytic.title: Adaptive Multi-Core Real-Time Scheduling Based on Reinforcement Learning

application.desc: GROBID - A machine learning software for extracting information from scholarly documents

div.p: With the transformation towards industrial intelligence, multi-core processors are increasingly being applied in real-time networked control systems to ensure secure execution of sensing, computing and actuating tasks under time constraints. However, existing scheduling methods result in either low CPU utilization or many missed task deadlines in dynamic systems. In this paper, we propose a two-layer scheduling architecture to address this issue by fully exploring the complex dependency between real-time tasks. To be specific, the local layer determines task execution priorities considering both dependency between tasks and deadline constraints by utilizing a reinforcement learning approach. Moreover, to better utilize the parallel capabilities of multi-core processors and reduce temporal collisions, this paper minimizes the requested core count for the task set based on a greedy strategy. The global layer designs a scheduling algorithm based on the preempt method and provides schedulability analysis of multiple task sets. Experimental results validate the correctness of the proposed scheduling approach, and efficiency is demonstrated through comparisons with baseline method.

div.head: I. INTRODUCTION
div.p: Real-time scheduling is fundamental to many safetycritical applications in real-time systems (RTSs). In modern RTSs, multi-core processors are used to meet growing demands for performance and functionality like parallel execution, particularly for intelligent application in networked control systems (NCSs) [7], [13]. Therefore, the Quality of Service (QoS) offered by a multi-core real-time scheduling strategy is not only the correctness of results and satisfaction of deadline, but also the multi-core resource utilization.

A typical NCS encompasses both computing component(s) for executing tasks like reasoning the control law, and sensing/operating component(s) for interaction with the environment. Tasks executed on computing components are typically periodic, and there are dependencies between tasks, for example, sensor data needs to be filtered in time before it can be used for control computation. Therefore, they must be completed under real-time and dependencies constraints with each execution. When multiple tasks contend for computing resources, it is necessary to control their resource usage priority and execution time by real-time scheduling to ensure the safety. Computing devices based on single-core processors are extensively used and the real-time scheduling theory for such systems have been researched matured [9]. Recently, there is a growing trend that high-performance multi-core processors are deployed for the challenges of intelligent transformation of NCSs. However, task scheduling in multicore systems is recognized as one of the most complex issues, which often is considered NP-Hard [8].

Traditionally, real-time task scheduling is performed during the application design [12]. It is simple to implement and provides stable execution, but cannot adapt to dynamic changes in workload, which may result in either low CPU utilization or many missed task deadlines in dynamic systems. Current research is focused on dynamic scheduling, achieved by generating scheduling strategies during runtime [3]. But the time cost of searching for the optimal scheduling strategy is deemed unacceptable because of the vast searching space. To cope with such challenges, numerous heuristic approaches have been proposed to search feasible solutions rapidly [16], [10]. These heuristic methods do not rely on any prior analysis results, thus providing relatively low-quality scheduling strategies. However, they rely on the design of heuristic rules and careful selection of parameters, which may lead to significant performance variations. In contrast, scheduling methods based on prior analysis results can achieve better quality. For example, a typical two-level hierarchical scheduling framework (HSF) generates scheduling strategy at the local level off-line and selects resource to run at the global level on-line, but it requires knowledge of all applications in advance to perform the analysis [6], [1]. Reinforcement Learning (RL) based algorithms for solving scheduling problems have gained increasing attention [4], [2], [11], which typically defines an agent that interacts with an unknown environment, aiming to maximize rewards [5]. RL-based algorithms are considering both immediate and long-term rewards, which are more likely to get better performance and avoid falling into a local optimum. However, most of those work only focus on independent tasks, and the scheduling of multi-core resources are not taken into full consideration.

Considering these problems, this paper proposes a twolevel RL-based hierarchical scheduling method for multicore NCSs that effectively utilizes computational resources. The local layer operates offline with the objective of meeting the deadline and dependency constraints of tasks set while minimizing the occupation of cores. The global layer operates online, aiming to perform admission control for the task sets and provides global scheduling strategies. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach can schedule the tasks correctly, while getting better performance and efficiency versus the baseline.

The paper is organized as follows. In Section II the task model is explained and the problem is formulated. Section III introduces the RL-based scheduling method. Section IV conducts experiments to demonstrate the correctness and effectiveness of the scheduling method. Section V gives the conclusions.

div.head: II. PROBLEM FORMULATION
div.p: Consider an NCS with sensors, a multi-core controller, and actuators, see Fig. 1 for an illustration of visual servoing for the robotic arms. The sensors acquire environmental information and send it to the controller for analysis and computation. The computed results are control inputs which are transmitted to the actuators to perform actions. The secure operation of the NCS relies on the timely analysis of data and the computation of instructions. Each application consists of several computing tasks that have a common deadline to accomplish a specific mission. It may involve the execution of a series of consecutive real-time computing tasks on the controller, characterized by data dependencies that must strictly follow a strict order and time requirements.

Let the task set be AP P = {App 1 , App 2 , ..., App s } on the CP U = {Core max } of the multi-core controller, where App is a real-time application, the Core max represents the maximum number of cores that can be allocated to tasks from the CP U , dependencies may exist among sub-tasks of each independent App.

Each App can be represented by a tuple (ϕ, D, T, n, τ , W , DEP ), where ϕ, D, T , n are scalars denoted as the phase, relative deadline, period, and the number of sub-tasks. τ is a n dimension vector, where τ i is the i th sub-task, composed of the worst-case execution time (WCET) workload of processor unit time w i , i = 1, ..., n, W is the vector form of sub-tasks workload. DEP represents the dependency of sub-tasks as an n × n matrix composed of 0, 1, where 1 in the i th row and j th column indicates that the i th sub-task is dependent on the j th sub-task. Only when the i th task is completed can the j th task be executed.

As shown in Fig. 1, the visual servoing AP P = {App 1 , App 2 , App 3 } system is employed to control the motion of three robotic arms, each application comprising sub-tasks of a similar structure but different workloads. The meanings of each sub-task in the diagram are as follows. τ 1 and τ 4 : Image filtering and rectification for stereo camera images; τ 5 : Feature extraction; τ 2 : Shape detection and disparity calculation; τ 3 : Depth calculation; τ 6 : Motion planning and control computation. Arrows indicate dependencies. There are some independent auxiliary tasks, such as distancebased emergency braking, denoted as τ 7 to τ n , that must be completed within the deadline.

The objective of the scheduling problem is to determine the execution order of each sub-task within the application to meet the dependencies DEP under the deadline constraint D, and allocate computing resources to AP P while avoiding conflicts between tasks.

As there are no dependencies among the Apps in AP P set, in order to optimize the parallel capabilities of multicore systems and minimize the probability of time collision, the scheduling problem can be formulated in a dual-layer structure. The local layer operates offline to meet the deadline and dependency constraints of App by solving the execution priority of n sub-tasks, while minimizing the occupation of cores. The global layer operates online, aiming to perform admission control for the App in AP P set, allocate the cores, and resolve conflicts.

Our objective in this paper is to determine the scheduling strategy rapidly, while avoiding the local optimal.

div.head: III. RL-BASED TWO-LAYER SCHEDULING METHOD
div.p: In this section, the scheduling method is described in detail. The aim of offline scheduling is to minimize the core required by App while satisfying deadline and subtasks dependency constraints, and the objective of online scheduling is performing admission control for the App and ensure that the AP P set meets deadline constraints.

div.head: A. Strategy Iteration for Offline Scheduling
div.p: In the local scheduling of the App, we consider the arrangement sub-tasks, where their dependency and deadline constraints are only related to their priorities. However, the search space for the combination of sub-tasks is vast. Traditional methods such as heuristic approaches often struggle with the extensive search time, for instance, considering an App with 15 sub-tasks and 8 available cores, there are 15! × 8 ≈ 10 13 possible scheduling plans in total.
In this paper, we adopt the RL method to rapidly search and avoid local optima. RL is a Markov decision process closely associated with state space S, action space A, and reward R.

div.head: 4) Policy:
div.p: The policy π is a conditional probability π(S|A), indicating which action to take given a state. In this paper, a two-layer neural network is used to estimate the policy, which essentially serves as the local offline scheduler. The neural network is denoted as π(θ), where θ represents the parameters. The state s is fed into π(θ) to calculate the probabilities of taking each action, then, a with the highest probability is selected for execution. Once the training is complete, with a given random priority list of sub-tasks in App, the scheduler can generate a scheduling strategy under constraints.

When a new App arrives, it first occupies idle cores. If all cores are in an occupied state, the scheduler sequentially compares the deadlines of arriving App and running App across all cores. It selects the App with the latest deadline to execute. When the preempted App will miss its deadline, the remaining portion of the arriving App will occupy the core of the running App with the largest laxity.

Based on these two layers, an AP P set can be well scheduled to meet the dependency and deadline constraints of each App.

div.head: IV. PERFORMANCE EVALUATION
div.p: In this section, we evaluate the performance of the proposed method. Firstly, we conduct scheduling experiments on the robotic arm visual servoing scenario to validate the effectiveness of the proposed method. Subsequently, it is compared with the baseline method Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) [15] to verify the efficiency of the proposed RL-based local scheduling method.

div.head: A. Experimental Setup
div.p: For the scheduling of robotic arm visual servoing applications, tasks information is presented in the TABLE I, where DEP {1} means the index tuple of DEP that the element equals to 1. We construct a test set consisting of 100 real-time applications. Scheduled by the CP U can providing up to 8 cores. Each App comprises 1 to 50 sub-tasks. The workload of each sub-task is described by the amount of unit time of CPU, randomly chosen from [1,20]. Dependencies are randomly generated between sub-tasks, with the maximum count equal to the number of sub-tasks. For comparison purpose, we set the swarm size of the baseline PSO to 200, the dim is set to n. Values for the cognitive parameter, social parameter, and inertia weight are typically chosen from the intervals [0, 4], [0,4], and [0, 1], respectively. In this experiment, we have set them as 2, 2, and 0.8, respectively. The experiments are conducted on the Lenovo Y9000-P laptop, which has an Intel 12900H CPU and 16 GB RAM. If the training offline scheduling in Algorithm 1 lasts for 20 episodes without a change in reward, we stop it.

div.head: B. Experimental Results
div.p: In the first experiment, we initialize App 1-4 according to Table I, where App 1-3 corresponds to the example illustrated in Fig. 1. Their local scheduling strategies are based on the offline part of Algorithm 1, which calculates both subtask priorities and the minimum of required core(s). Core req and the average action reward are shown in Fig. 2. During the training of App 1-4 , the requested cores stabilize to the minimum value of 3,3,2,2, respectively. The average action reward per episodic fluctuates initially, indicating the agent exploration. As described in Equation (11) to Equation ( 13), when all constraints are satisfied, R ds equals 10, and R oc is related to Core req . The maximum reward of each action for App 1 and App 2 are 13, while for App 3 and App 4 , the maximum reward is 15. At the stable state, the agent tends to execute the least action, i.e. 1 step, that do not violate dependencies. Based on the priorities and Core req , Algorithm 1 is applied to obtain the scheduling result as shown in Fig. 3, where τ j,k i denotes the i th sub-task in j th instance of App i , the dependencies between sub-tasks are indicated by dashed lines in the first instance of each App. It can be observed that App 1-3 with complex constraints, occupy the least cores, allowing for effective parallel processing and avoiding the time collisions. When App 4 arrives at t = 12, it takes a schedulability test based on Equation (19), the result is 0.97 that is less than 1. Thus it is permitted entry into the system and scheduling. With the arrival of τ 4,1 , it initially occupies the free core 7 and 8. When τ 3,2 arrives at t = 17, it is scheduled to start execution at t = 19, as τ 4,1 has an earlier deadline. When τ 2,3 arrives at t = 22, due to the earlier deadline of τ 4,2 , τ 2,3 is postponed. However, at t = 25, the completion time of the last sub-task of τ 2,3 coincides with the deadline, leading to preemption of subtasks of τ 3,2 by τ 2 and τ 4 . It is clear that all the Apps meet deadline and dependency constraints. The scheduling results validate the correctness of the scheduling strategy proposed in this paper. In the second experiment. We compare the scheduling solutions obtained using the proposed method with those obtained using a PSO based method [15]. The maximum iteration count for RL is set to 100, and the maximum iteration count for PSO is set to 10,000.

We utilize the mentioned application set in the experimental setup, categorizing them into five classes based on the sub-tasks amount of the App. The results demonstrate that the proposed method performs remarkably well in randomly generated sets of tasks with complex constraints. The percentage of finding feasible solutions in the five categories are 100%, 77%, 77%, 70%, and 75%, respectively, surpassing the PSO-based method comprehensively. The runtime for finding feasible solutions is presented in Table II. It can be observed that, compared with the PSO-based method, the proposed algorithm can provide feasible solutions within 1 second for small-scale Apps. Even in an extremely large search space (up to 2.4 × 10 65 in this case), the search time is controlled to around 10 seconds, which validates V. CONCLUSIONS In this paper, we have studied scheduling problem for multi-core real-time NCS systems of real-time task sets with complex dependency constraints under real-time constraints. A two-layer scheduling method is proposed. At the local layer, task execution priorities are determined based on reinforcement learning to meet constraints and minimize the occupied core count, thereby improving the utilization of the parallel capabilities of multi-core processor. The global layer provides admission control criteria and schedulability analysis. Experimental results validate the correctness of the proposed scheduling approach and demonstrate its superior performance compared to baseline (PSO) across tasks of different scales.
